newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan backs umbrella regulator for big firms.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan backs umbrella regulator for big firms.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday backed consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates but said the central bank does not have to play the role of umbrella regulator in all cases.
"You do need some form of regulatory entity which has consolidated supervision (responsibilities)," he told the House Banking Committee.
But he said that the umbrella regulator should be the Securities and Exchnage Commission, not the Fed, when most of a financial conglomerate's business is in securities, rather than in banking.
"If most of the (conglomerate's) subsidiaries are securities-type subsidiaries and the bank is a small part, then I would say the consolidating supervisor should be the SEC," Greenspan said.
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt told the Committee that he opposed consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates. "I don't believe you need an umbrella supervisor," he said.

The question of whether or not an umbrella supervisor is needed -- and who it should be -- has come to the fore as Congress considers breaking down the walls separating banks, insurance companies and securities firms.
